His twelve were checkable actions: rise early, sit in stillness, read one book at a time, keep the diary, note what was said over tea, let no month pass forgetting what he could do. Small enough to judge today. Being seen is the cheapest constraint — Circulating the diary cost him almost nothing and did far more than resolve did. This is not performance, it is deliberately importing an outside correction, because a person's estimate of himself always runs high and honesty alone will not bring it down. Where you are: you have set the goal many
q: Watchfulness when alone brings peace of mind.
Steady work that never breaks off beats a burst of courage.

chapters.w: Judge people inside real work
chapters.dek: A great many provincial governors came out of his staff. This asks how he judged a man before the man had anything to show.
chapters.txt: His method had two halves. Taking in widely meant a low bar at the door: bring people onto the staff and keep the pool large. Employing carefully moved the bar to the far end — not the record and not the conversation, but a real piece of work handed over, and then watching how he judged under actual pressure, how he reported, and what he did with the part he could not do. Li Hongzhang came up exactly that way, from the staff to independent command. What he looked for all his life was principle without officialdom, order in the head and few big words. Widen the entrance, tighten the exit — Selecting hard at the door assumes you can see through a man in one conversation, and that assumption usually does not hold. Moving the weight of the filter onto the first real task costs less and judges considerably better. Watch how he accounts for it, not how it ended — A thing that came off may have come off by luck. What exposes a person is the process: whether he raises the part he cannot do early or holds it to the end, whether detail questions find him solid or vague, whether a failure comes back as a cause or as an excuse. Few big words — Principle without officialdom, order in the head and few big words. He was wary of two kinds: the man whose manner exceeds his content, and the man whose talk exceeds his work. The first drains an organisation and the second manufactures
q: Principle without officialdom, order in the head and few big words.
For great undertakings, finding successors is the first business.

chapters.w: Hang every item on a name and a date
chapters.dek: Orders go down and nobody carries them out. This is about the ledger he used to fix a failure every dynasty had.
chapters.txt: In 1573 he described the situation plainly: the memorials were endless and no office held to anything. Once an order left, nobody tracked it, and there was no record of whether it had been done. His fix was crude. Everything due was entered in a register, in three copies, with a deadline, and struck off item by item when it fell due. If the governors delay, the ministries report it; if the ministries conceal, the six offices report it; if the six offices miss it, we report it. Within a few years an order issued in the morning was obeyed by evening ten thousand li away. Issued is not finished; struck off is — Most organisations break in the same place: there is a record that the order went out and no record that it came back. Without the act of striking off, work evaporates between layers naturally, and nobody has to answer for the evaporation. The point of three copies is the third one — One copy stayed with the office, one went to the supervising bureau, one to the cabinet. The same item sits in three places that do not report to each other, so any attempt to soften it shows up in the other two. A single ledger never cures delay. The audit has to reach the top layer — The decisive clause is that if the supervising offices miss it, the cabinet reports them. Nearly every assessment system stops at the supervisors, which makes the supervisors the one link nobody checks, and the whole chain slackens
q: The memorials are endless and no office holds to anything.
If the six offices miss it, we report it ourselves.

chapters.w: Merge the accounts into one payment
chapters.dek: Why does the same sum shrink the more hands it passes through? This is about merging dozens of levies into one.
chapters.txt: Mid-Ming taxes and labour service were absurdly tangled: land tax, head service, tribute goods, labour levies, silver levies, dozens of headings, each with its own collection date, its own collector, its own conversion rate. Every stage was an opportunity to take a little more, and what the people paid and what the treasury received were far apart. The single whip totalled a county's taxes and services together, measured by land and counted by head, and all of it was paid in to the government. The state now hired labour for the year instead of levying it. Dozens of payments became one, in silver, on one date. Every stage is a chance to lose something — Complexity is itself a cost. More headings and more hands mean more room for interpretation, and every scrap of interpretive room eventually gets used. Simplification is not valuable because it saves effort; it is valuable because it removes the positions where things are done quietly. One unit of measurement — Converting to silver is the step people skip past, and it is the pivot of the whole reform. Goods, labour and time are not commensurable, so they cannot be reconciled. Once everything is in one unit, over-collection and under-collection are visible at a glance. Simplifying offends whoever lives on the complexity — Complexity did not arise by itself; it is useful to somebody. The single whip cut into exactly the clerks and gentry who profited from the stages, which is why he was condemned after his death — and why the law survived, because it
q: Total a county's taxes and services, measure by land, count by head.
A year's labour service, hired by the government instead.

chapters.n: The old man on the bridge
chapters.w: The test before the test
chapters.dek: An old man puts a young man through a series of pointless humiliations. The question worth asking is what was being tested.
chapters.txt: On the bridge at Xiapi an old man dropped his shoe over the side and told the young Zhang Liang to fetch it. He wanted to hit him, held off because of the man's age, brought it up, then knelt and put it on his foot. The old man walked away laughing and turned back to say the boy can be taught, then set a meeting at dawn five days on. Twice the old man was there first and furious. The third time Zhang Liang went at midnight and waited, and was given a book. What is tested is whether you can take an unreasonable rule — The old man never explains anything. He sets the terms alone and raises them whenever he likes. What Zhang Liang passes is not a test of temper but a harder practical judgement: with the rules unexplained and plainly unfair, going along still pays more than fighting. Restraint has a target — He was not a mild man. He had spent the family fortune to hire a strongman to hurl an iron club at the First Emperor's carriage. The same person would not endure an emperor and would endure an old man. Restraint is a verdict on the occasion, not a temperament. The third attempt was the right one — Both earlier times he thought he had come early and was still late. After the second failure he neither gave up nor argued about the standard. He raised his own by a notch and went at midnight. Most people stop at the second failure
q: The boy can be taught.
He had already fetched the shoe, so he knelt and fitted it on.

chapters.w: Take the plan apart into conditions
chapters.dek: A proposal sounds entirely right. How do you show that it is wrong? This is the method he ran at the table, in one sitting.
chapters.txt: Chu and Han were deadlocked and Liu Bang was shut up in Xingyang. The adviser Li Yiji proposed re-establishing the heirs of the six old states, who would be grateful, so that the empire would come over. Liu Bang liked it and ordered the seals cut. Zhang Liang came in, was told, and said let me borrow the chopsticks in front of you and lay this out for Your Majesty. Then eight items, each one a question about whether it could be done now. Liu Bang stopped eating and had the seals destroyed. Do not argue the conclusion, audit the premises — Li Yiji's conclusion, that enfeoffment buys allegiance, is nearly impossible to refute head on. Zhang Liang never tried. He broke it into the conditions it requires and asked of each whether it was available today. A plan that collapses at the condition layer stays collapsed. Put a physical object where the abstraction was — Borrowing the chopsticks turns a strategy into pieces on a table that people can point at. The value of that move is that it shifts the room from whether this is sound to how this would run. Almost every bad plan is sound. Very few of them run. If it is wrong, turn round now — The one who is really tested here is Liu Bang. He had already ordered the seals cut, heard eight objections, and destroyed them the same hour. Finding the flaw in a plan is the easy half. Withdrawing something you personally approved an hour ago is the other one.
q: Let me borrow the chopsticks in front of you and lay it out.
Take that man's advice and Your Majesty's cause is finished.

chapters.w: Asking for the small thing at the summit
chapters.dek: You are told to name your own reward. Do you take the largest one available? Here is why he took the smallest.
chapters.txt: With the empire settled, Liu Bang told him to choose thirty thousand households anywhere in Qi, the highest grant then possible. He declined. He had raised troops at Xiapi and met His Majesty at Liu, and that meeting was heaven's doing: enfeoff me at Liu and it is enough; I dare not accept thirty thousand households. Liu was a small county. He then pleaded illness, took up the regimen and gave up grain, saying he wished to drop the affairs of men. Of that founding generation Han Xin was killed and Peng Yue destroyed. Zhang Liang died in his bed. Asking for the small thing is a signal — Thirty thousand households is not money, it is a base with its own revenue and its own men. What he turned down was the structure, not the wealth. Choosing a small county announces in public that he does not intend to grow into a problem somebody will eventually have to solve. Give the other side a version it can repeat — He did not say he was afraid of being suspected. He said Liu was where they met and that heaven had arranged it. The true reason spoken aloud would have shamed them both. Offering a version everyone can live with is not insincerity, it is leaving people room to move. Leave while people still want you to stay — He began withdrawing at the point of maximum credit and maximum usefulness. The timing and the proceeds of an exit run in opposite directions: the later you leave, the less there
q: Enfeoff me at Liu. That is enough. I dare not take thirty thousand.
I wish to drop the affairs of men and follow Master Red Pine.

chapters.w: The trait he rates highest
chapters.dek: Asked which quality he values, he keeps giving one answer. What the phrase actually means in his hands.
chapters.txt: In interviews Zhang Yiming has said that delayed gratification is one of the qualities I value most, and that graduates who put never losing out first are spending themselves in advance. In his usage the phrase covers three layers. Choosing work: do not trade the fastest-growing seat for this year's salary. Building product: hold off monetising, as early Toutiao pushed commercialisation back and worked the recommendation engine and retention first. For the company: refuse to be satisfied by the result of the current fight. His own gloss on the reverse side is that most people want too badly to win the round in front of them. What is delayed is the payout, not the feedback — The common misuse is to invoke it while enduring years with no signal at all. In his practice the feedback is immediate, data watched daily, retention chased daily, and only the conversion into money and reputation is postponed. Delay with feedback is investment; delay without it is self-admiration. Cashing in early has a hidden price: compounding stops — The cost of early monetising never shows on the statement. Damage the experience for this period's revenue and you shrink the base that every later period grows from. The trait is really a compound-interest sum: move the payout later so the principal turns more times. People who can do the arithmetic need no willpower. It is a filter for choosing people, not only a private discipline — He applies the trait in hiring, by looking at a candidate's past choices: always the highest current pay, or
q: Delayed gratification is one of the qualities I value most.
Most people want too badly to win the round in front of them.

chapters.n: An ordinary mind for extraordinary things
chapters.w: The ninth-anniversary speech
chapters.dek: A company known for ferocity spent its ninth anniversary on composure. The specific kinds of interference he named.
chapters.txt: At ByteDance's ninth anniversary in 2021 Zhang Yiming's all-hands had a single theme: keep an ordinary mind while doing extraordinary things. He named the common distortions. Toward the past, vanity about achievements or self-pity about setbacks. Toward competition, watching the rival so closely that the rival leads you. Toward the future, targets set so far from reality that anxiety eats the effort. His argument is that lifting attention off the patterns and the noise and seeing the present as it is produces better judgement. Extraordinary results come from an ordinary state of mind held at the decisive moments. Watching the rival hands over the steering wheel — Excess attention to competition means the agenda gets taken over: they ship and you answer, they attack and you defend. It looks like fighting back, but you are already executing their strategy for them. Composure here is concrete. A rival's move is one input, and its weight should not exceed your own user data. Vanity and self-pity are the same coin — Pairing them is exact. Pride in past success and grief over a setback run on the same mechanism, with attention locked on me rather than on the thing. Decisions made in either state serve a self-image: one proving it still has it, the other proving it was unfair. Targets within reach keep anxiety from taking over — A target detached from reality does not produce drive, it produces anxiety, and anxiety distorts judgement systematically: short horizons inflated, fundamentals skipped, remedies grabbed at random. Composure is not the absence of ambition. It
q: Keep an ordinary mind while doing extraordinary things.
Watch your rival too closely and you end up being led.

chapters.n: Be slow to take the title
chapters.w: Do without the name for now
chapters.dek: Everyone who rose at the same time was claiming a throne. He was the one who did not, and it was worth eleven years.
chapters.txt: In 1357, having taken Huizhou, he went to see the old scholar Zhu Sheng and asked how to settle the empire. Zhu Sheng gave him nine characters: build the walls high, store the grain widely, be slow to take the title. Around him, Han Lin'er was the Little Prince of Brightness, Xu Shouhui had declared himself emperor, Zhang Shicheng was the Prince of Cheng, Chen Youliang would call himself emperor of Han. Everyone with strength was grabbing a name. He followed the nine characters for eleven years, while the Yuan armies spent them on the men who had claimed first. A title is an act of switching your own light on — The name brings a power to summon people, and it also gives your coordinates. The moment the title is hung on you, you stop being a roving band and become a regime that has to be destroyed first. Before you can absorb concentrated fire, a name is a liability. The three go together, or not at all — High walls are the ability to defend, wide stores the ability to last, slow titles the ability to stay unlit. The third alone is just hiding; the first two alone are a large obvious target. Because you are accumulating and can hold, you have earned the right to wait. When to claim it is a separate judgement — Slow does not mean never. He waited until Chen Youliang and Zhang Shicheng had both been destroyed, the Yuan court was fighting itself, and the whole south was his. The test was
q: Build the walls high, store the grain widely, be slow to take the title.
The day the title goes up, your coordinates go up with it.

chapters.w: A broken age needs a heavy hand
chapters.dek: He put officials to death by the tens of thousands. This is about how he himself defined the range this method applied to.
chapters.txt: He was merciless about corruption: an official who took sixty taels was executed, and each prefectural and county yamen had a skinning ground beside it, the stuffed skin set next to the seat of office. He compiled the Grand Pronouncements, printed the actual cases, distributed them across the empire, required every household to keep a copy and put them in the examinations. When the heir said the punishments were too heavy, the History of Ming records his answer: I govern a broken age, so the punishments cannot but be heavy. You will govern a settled one, and yours can be light. Heavy punishment is for resetting expectations — By the end of the Yuan, administration had collapsed and officials generally assumed that graft had no consequences. To break that assumption the penalty has to be heavy enough that everyone recalculates. It is a one-off cost of resetting, not a way to run things — he said so himself. Cases travel further than clauses — The Grand Pronouncements printed real cases rather than abstract statutes: who, where, what they did, what happened to them. An abstract rule makes each reader work out whether it applies to him; a case hands him the comparison directly, and costs far less to spread. He set an expiry date and nobody honoured it — Inside I govern a broken age there is a self-limit: the method has conditions, and when they go it should go. The trouble is that severity, once institutionalised, will not leave on its own — it grows an enforcement apparatus that
q: I govern a broken age, so the punishments cannot but be heavy.
You will govern a settled age, and your punishments can be light.

chapters.w: What nobody requisitions lives longest
chapters.dek: Making yourself useful is instinct. What being useful costs you at the same time.
chapters.txt: A master carpenter passes an oak so vast it could shade thousands of oxen, and doesn't look twice. Asked why, he says: it's useless timber — boats from it sink, coffins rot, tools break. Good for nothing, and so it has lived this long. That night the tree comes to him in a dream: the fruit trees get torn apart the moment the fruit ripens; their ability is what harms them. I have sought uselessness a long time, and only now have it. Then Zhuangzi turns it on people: everyone knows the use of the useful; nobody knows the use of the useless. Useful is a qualification to be requisitioned — Once a person is judged unusually good at something, that something arrives without end. It looks like being valued. It is being fixed in one position and spent there — the ability itself becomes the source of the load. Useless is the room you keep for yourself — The useless tree survived by not appearing on anyone's list. People need a portion of time and ability that isn't counted as output — it produces nothing immediately, and it is the only part nobody else gets to schedule. Don't exhaust yourself in a single position — Zhuangzi isn't against being useful. He's against being useful as the only way of existing. Used to the limit means completely defined, and the moment that use isn't wanted the person expires with it. Where you are: you're the one on the team who can carry anything, and you're busier every month. Ask first:
q: Good for nothing, and so it has lived this long.
Everyone knows the use of the useful. Nobody knows the use of the useless.

chapters.w: Go along the gaps
chapters.dek: One cook replaces his blade monthly, another hasn't in nineteen years. Where exactly the difference sits.
chapters.txt: Cook Ding carves an ox for Lord Wenhui and the movement looks like dancing. Asked how his technique got so good, he says what he cares about isn't technique. At first he saw a whole ox; after three years he no longer saw a whole ox; now he meets it with the spirit rather than looking with the eye. A good cook changes his blade yearly, because he cuts. An ordinary one monthly, because he hacks. His has done thousands of oxen in nineteen years and the edge is as if newly whetted — because he has been travelling in the gaps between the joints. The blade stays sharp because it never meets the hard part — The edge has no thickness and the joints have space; something thin entering something wide moves easily. Struggle isn't a shortage of force. It's the wrong place to put the blade. Every hard collision is a positioning problem. See the structure before you talk about technique — Ding's three stages — seeing a whole ox, ceasing to see a whole ox, meeting it with the spirit — are increasingly fine readings of structure. Technique is a by-product of that reading. Train it in the other order and you are training force. Slow down where it knots — Ding isn't smooth throughout: at every knot he sees the difficulty, grows wary, slows, and makes his movements smaller. Real fluency isn't speed the whole way. It's knowing where you must go slowly. Where you are: something is hard to push at every point, and you're
q: The joints have space, the blade has no thickness.
At every knot I see the difficulty, grow wary, and slow down.

chapters.w: Whose ruler is this
chapters.dek: Two people argue to the end and neither is convinced. Why Zhuangzi says a third person won't settle it either.
chapters.txt: Zhuangzi asks an almost mischievous question. A person sleeping somewhere damp gets a bad back — does a loach? A person up a tree is frightened — is a monkey? Of the three, who knows the proper place to live? He extends the logic to argument: if you beat me in a debate, are you actually right? Bring a third person to judge, and whether they agree with you or with me they have already taken a side. How could they settle it? This isn't abolishing right and wrong. It's a reminder that right and wrong always speak from inside some standard. Before arguing, ask whose ruler is being used — There is a right and wrong on that side too, and one on this side. Most deadlocks aren't disputes about facts, they're disputes about standards — each conclusion holds inside its own. Until the standards are on the table, no amount of discussion converges. The third party brings a standard too — Calling in a more senior person looks neutral and is really introducing a third standard. It ends the argument by authority rather than by understanding, so the same disagreement reappears unchanged the next time. Move position and the ruler changes — Zhuangzi's method isn't finding the one correct ruler. It's acknowledging where your own came from. Do that and the other conclusion stops being 'wrong' and becomes 'true under his conditions' — and then you can discuss conditions instead of correctness. Where you are: a disagreement keeps recurring and never resolves. Ask first: what is each side
q: There is a right and wrong on that side, and one on this side.
If you beat me in the argument, are you actually right?

chapters.w: The first half is what not to touch
chapters.dek: A twenty-seven-year-old lays out a strategy that governs the next several decades. Its hardest work is done in the opening section.
chapters.txt: Asked for a plan after the third visit, he began not with what to attack but with what could not be. Cao Cao has a million men and holds the emperor: you cannot contend with him. Sun Quan has held the east for three generations, the ground is hard and the people attached: he can be an ally, not a target. Two of the three biggest pieces on the board are crossed off before anything is chosen. Only then the available ones, Jing and Yi, and the conditions: hold both, keep the alliance, put the government in order, and when there is a change, move by two roads. The first half of a strategy is elimination — Rule out what cannot be beaten and what should not be touched, and what remains is the actual menu. Most strategy discussions skip the step and open with what we should do, which spreads the money across several fights that were never worth entering. Different relations for different stronger parties — Both are out of reach, and he treats them differently: one cannot be contended with, the other can be an ally but not a target. Filing everyone stronger than you under enemy is how a plan ends up isolated. Naming which one must be joined is what makes it stand. Write the trigger condition down — When there is a change in the empire is the whole plan's trigger. He never claims a date. He says that until the condition appears, everything being done is preparation. Writing the trigger down stops both
q: You cannot contend with him.
He can be made an ally. He cannot be taken.

chapters.n: Near the worthy, far from the small
chapters.w: It is about who can reach you alone
chapters.dek: Eight characters usually read as a moral instruction. What he means is narrower and more mechanical: who is able to see you privately.
chapters.txt: The memorial states it as cause and effect. Keeping near to worthy officials and far from small men is why the Former Han rose; the reverse is why the Later Han fell. Then, instead of moral advice, he arranges channels. Palace and government office are one body; reward and punishment must not differ between them. On matters in the palace, consult Guo Youzhi, Fei Yi and Dong Yun. On matters in the camp, consult Xiang Chong. And a warning: do not belittle yourself, and so block the road along which honest advice arrives. Near and far describe a channel, not a preference — A small man is not effective because he flatters well. He is effective because he holds a route to the decision maker that nobody else has. Cut the route and the same person has no influence at all. The thing to manage is the structure, not the character. Belittling yourself blocks the road too — Do not belittle yourself and so block the road of honest advice is the half nobody quotes. A leader who keeps saying he does not understand and is not much good leaves people unable to judge what is worth reporting, so they report less. Excessive modesty and deafness produce the same silence. Name the people and the subjects — He does not say listen to good advisers. He pairs names with subject matter, one line at a time: for this class of question, that man. Named to a person, the channel is real. Left as a principle, the channel is decorative. Where
q: Near the worthy and far from the small men: that is why they rose.
Do not belittle yourself and block the road honest advice comes along.

chapters.n: The tears, and then the demotion
chapters.w: He put himself on the same list
chapters.dek: Executing the man he had promoted is not the hard part of this story. What he did immediately afterwards is.
chapters.txt: On the first northern campaign he passed over Wei Yan and Wu Yi, whom everyone had recommended, and gave the vanguard to Ma Su. At Jieting Ma Su went against the deployment, left the water and camped on the hill; Zhang He cut the water off and destroyed him. Back in Hanzhong, Zhuge Liang executed him to answer to the army. Then he sent up a memorial asking to be demoted three ranks, with the charge spelt out: I was not clear-sighted about men, and muddled in handling affairs. He went from chancellor to general of the right. Punish only the executor and the fault leaks downward — The error happened in execution, but the choosing and the authorising happened above it. Handling the executor alone announces that the deciding layer carries no consequences, so the same failure returns by the same route, because the cause was never touched. Self-demotion has to name the charge — He did not say responsibility rests with me too. He wrote the specific count: not clear-sighted about men. That is a charge somebody can hold up against his later behaviour. Vague self-criticism binds nobody. A named one gets remembered and used. Weep, and carry out the law — He was as close to Ma Su as to a son and executed him anyway; then mourned him personally and raised his children. Feeling and rule each ran their own course at full strength. Using the feeling to suspend the rule, or the rule to prove you have no feeling, is half a job either. Where
q: He executed Ma Su to answer to the army.
I was not clear-sighted about men, and muddled in handling affairs.

chapters.w: The dangerous man is the able one
chapters.dek: The first argument in the first book of the whole work is about choosing people. This is about why it sits there.
chapters.txt: The book opens with the partition of Jin, and its first great event is the fall of Zhibo. Zhibo had five qualities above other men — bearing, horsemanship, skill, eloquence, decision — and one lack: he was not humane. On this Sima Guang hangs the first of his own comments. Talent is the resource of character; character is the commander of talent. He sorts people into four: both complete is a sage, both absent is a fool, character over talent is a gentleman, talent over character is a small man. Then blunt advice: failing a sage or a gentleman, take the fool. Talent is an amplifier; character sets the direction — Character commands, talent supplies — the image means talent has no direction of its own. The same ability doubles the return in a right direction and doubles the loss in a wrong one. So the stronger the person, the larger the damage when the direction is wrong. That is arithmetic, not moralising. A fool's damage has a ceiling — His reasoning is utilitarian. A fool who wants to do harm lacks the means and is easy to guard against; a capable man of bad character does harm nobody can stop. Where you cannot judge conduct, choosing the lower ceiling of ability is a way of capping the worst case. The trouble is that we see talent first — He names the root: talent is easy to see and character is not. An interview can measure ability and cannot measure where someone stops; a record can list the wins and
q: Talent is the resource of character; character is the commander of talent.
Character over talent is a gentleman, talent over character a small man.

chapters.w: Fix the selection rule first
chapters.dek: One thousand three hundred and sixty-two years of events. This is about the single rule that decided what went in.
chapters.txt: He ran the compilation for nineteen years and the finished work runs to two hundred and ninety-four volumes. In the memorial presenting it he set out how he chose: cut what was long-winded, gather what was essential, take only what bears on the rise and fall of the state, on whether the people prospered or suffered, what is good enough to copy and bad enough to warn. Shenzong, naming it, called it a mirror of what has been, useful to the art of governing. One rule throughout, which is why there is almost no ornament and almost nothing kept for completeness. Set the rule first or you never finish — Nineteen years, thirteen centuries of material: without a selection rule you can apply mechanically, the work is infinite. Take only is the condition that let the book be completed. He did not know what to write; he knew clearly what not to. The rule has to admit the bad — Bad enough to warn stands beside good enough to copy. A library of successes only teaches that there is one road that works. Failures usually carry more information, because a success can be accidental in many ways and a failure's mechanism is generally clearer. The rule has to be executable by someone else — The work was divided between Liu Ban, Liu Shu and Fan Zuyu, with Sima Guang over the whole. A taste that exists only in the editor's head cannot be divided. Only a rule written down and applied identically by three people will hold for nineteen years.
q: Cut what is long-winded; gather what is essential.
Good enough to copy, bad enough to warn.
